(predecessor FSK Daugava 90 founded in {{start date and age|May 19, 2005}}) | ground = [[LNK Sporta Parks]] | capacity = 2,300 | chairman = [[Artjoms Milovs]] | manager = [[Viktors Morozs]] | league = [[Latvian Higher League|Virslīga]] | season = [[2025 Latvian Higher League|2025]] | position = [[Latvian Higher League|Virslīga]], 2nd of 10 | current = 2024 FK RFS season | pattern_la1 = _nikevapor5gr | pattern_b1 = _nikevapor5gr | pattern_ra1 = _nikevapor5gr | pattern_sh1 = _nikevapor5gr | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = 0000FF | body1 = 0000FF | rightarm1 = 0000FF | shorts1 = 0000FF | socks1 = 0000FF | pattern_la2 = _nikeprecision7w | pattern_b2 = _nikeprecision7w | pattern_ra2 = _nikeprecision7w | pattern_sh2 = | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = FFFFFF | socks2 = FFFFFF | pattern_la3 = _nikestrike4bv25 | pattern_b3 = _nikestrike4bv25 | pattern_ra3 = _nikestrike4bv25 | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = 000000 | body3 = 000000 | rightarm3 = 000000 | shorts3 = CCFF00 | socks3 = CCFF00 | website = {{URL|https://fkrfs.lv/en/|fkrfs.lv}} }} '''FK RFS''' (also '''FC RFS''') is a professional [[Latvia]]n [[association football|football]] club based in [[Riga]]. The club competes in the Virslīga, the top tier of [[Football in Latvia|Latvian football]]. It has existed in its current form since 2016, with predecessors dating back to 2005. The team traditionally wears a blue home kit and a white away kit. After spending its first six years at [[Jānis Skredelis' Stadium|Jānis Skredelis Stadium]], RFS has played at the privately funded [[LNK Sporta Parks]] since 2022. RFS has won the Latvian championship three times ([[2021 Latvian Higher League|2021]], [[2023 Latvian Higher League|2023]], [[2024 Latvian Higher League|2024]]) and the [[Latvian Football Cup|Latvian Cup]] three times ([[2019 Latvian Football Cup|2019]], [[2021 Latvian Football Cup|2021]], [[2024 Latvian Football Cup|2024]]). In 2022, the club was named Best Sports Club in Riga. That year, RFS became only the second Latvian club to qualify for the group stage of a European competition, following [[2009 FK Ventspils season|Ventspils in 2009–10]], after defeating [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]] in the [[UEFA Conference League|UEFA Europa Conference League]] play-off. In January 2025, RFS recorded the first-ever victory by a Latvian club in a UEFA group stage, defeating [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]]."}}
